full_judgment:
Sheikh Hassan Arif J : Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 5-7-2017 (decree signed on 12-7-2017) passed by the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Bogura in Artha Rin Suit No. 38 of 2016 under section 13(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, should not be declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 2. Facts, relevant for the disposal of the Rule, are that National Credit & Commerce Bank Limited, through its Bogura Branch (respondent No.2), filed Artha Rin Suit No. 38 of 2016 before the Artha Rin Adalat, Boruga against the petitioner and another for realization of loan amount of Taka 3,87,73,120. In the said suit, the petitioner was impleaded as defendant No.1, being proprietor of M/s Samvunath Kundu. To contest the said suit, the petitioner filed written statement and thereafter filed application for framing of issues for trial of the suit. Thereupon, the Adalat passed the impugned judgment and decree vide order dated 5-7-2017 purportedly under section 13(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 on the ground that the petitioner did not deny the claims of the plaintiff and that there was nothing in the pleadings to frame issues for proceeding with the trial. Being aggrieved by such judgment and decree, the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the aforesaid Rule. At the time of issuance of the Rule, this Court, vide ad-interim order dated 23-8-2017, stayed operation of the said judgment and decree dated 5-7-2017 for a period of 3 (three) months, which was subsequently extended for further periods. 

 4. Mr Hafizur Rahman, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner, at the outset of the hearing, has drawn this Court's attention to the averments of the plaintiff in the plaint and the averments of the defendant-petitioner in the written statement as annexed to the writ petition as Annexures A and B. Learned advocate submits that the material averments and claims in the plaint as regards liability and default as well as demands against the petitioner have been categorically denied by the petitioner in the written statement filed by him. Therefore, according to him, this case was not a fit case to deliver judgment without trial or without framing issues in view of the provisions under sub-section (1) of section 13 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Learned advocate submits that even the petitioner has filed an application for framing of issues suggesting some issues therein. However, he submits, the Adalat ignored such intention of the petitioner to face the trial and decreed the suit thereby depriving the petitioner of his legal entitlement to contest the said suit as defendant. Learned advocate submits that this is a clear example of violation of principle of natural justice inasmuch as that the petitioner has been deprived of his right to contest the said suit in accordance with law. 

 5. As against above submissions, Mr Nasir Sikder, learned advocate appearing for the respondent bank, submits that no writ petition is maintainable against judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. This being so, according to him, this Court should discharge the Rule. 

 6. Since the Adalat has delivered the impugned judgment and decree purportedly under sub-section (1) of section 13 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, the said provision is quoted below for our ready reference: 

 12. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and decree dated 5-7-2017 is hereby set aside. The Adalat concerned is directed to frame issues in accordance with law after considering the pleadings and then proceed with the trial of the concerned suit in accordance with law.
